options.text: With a $15000$ RPM disk, the expected rotation time for a random access is $4$ ms.
Transfer time for disk sectors is significantly longer for random accesses than for sequential accesses.
Doubling the rotation speed of a disk also doubles the transfer rate.
The elevator algorithm does not take rotational time into account when scheduling I/O requests.

questions.solution:
Answer: A, B

Source solution 1 (score: 0)
Random access would take the average rotational delay and that would be 2msec and sequential access would take longer than random access because random access has to access 1 sector randomly but sequential access would have to access every sector on the track leading up to that sector. Please correct me if I am wrong.
Source solution 2 (score: 0)
 
The correct answer should be A and B.
A. False
For a 15000 RPM disk,
Time for one complete rotation = 60 / 15000 = 0.004 s = 4 ms.
However, for a random access, the expected (average) rotational latency is half a rotation, i.e., 2 ms, not 4 ms. Therefore, the statement is false because it uses the full rotation time instead of the average rotational latency.
B. False
The statement talks about transfer time, not access time.
Access Time = Seek Time + Rotational Latency + Transfer Time
Random access significantly increases seek time and rotational latency, but transfer time itself remains approximately the same for reading the same amount of data at the same disk speed. Hence, the statement is false. If it had said access time instead of transfer time, it would have been true.
C. True
Assuming the amount of data per rotation remains unchanged, doubling the disk's rotational speed doubles the number of rotations per second, thereby doubling the transfer rate.

Here's a simple numerical example you can use.

Example
Suppose a disk stores 100 KB of data in one complete rotation.
Case 1: Disk speed = 6000 RPM
  • 6000 RPM = 100 rotations/second
  • Data transferred per rotation = 100 KB
Transfer rate = 100 × 100 KB = 10,000 KB/s = 10 MB/s
Case 2: Disk speed = 12000 RPM (double the RPM)
  • 12000 RPM = 200 rotations/second
  • Data per rotation = 100 KB (unchanged)
Transfer rate = 200 × 100 KB = 20,000 KB/s = 20 MB/s
So,
  • RPM: 6000 → 12000 (2×)
  • Transfer rate: 10 MB/s → 20 MB/s (2×)
Hence, doubling the rotational speed doubles the transfer rate, assuming the amount of data read per rotation remains the same.
Therefore, if Data per Rotation is constant, then:
Transfer Rate ∝ RPM
D. True
The Elevator (SCAN) algorithm schedules requests based on cylinder numbers to minimize seek time. It does not consider the rotational position of sectors while scheduling I/O requests. Hence, rotational latency is not taken into account by the algorithm.
Therefore, the false statements are A and B only.
